newsitem.title: UK: JP Morgan starts Hang Seng as underperform.
newsitem.headline: JP Morgan starts Hang Seng as underperform.

text.p: Investment bank JP Morgan said on Tuesday it started coverage of Hang Seng Bank as "market underperformer", saying the bank's share price is overvalued and that a recent sharp rise is not supported by fundamentals.
It said the fact that Hang Seng is 62 percent owned by HSBC Holdings Plc means the bank has only a limited mandate to expand outside the highly competitive Hong Kong market.

"We believe that the bank will continue to lose market share and that asset growth will fall below industry levels -- the result of both Hang Seng's lack of overseas branches and of increased competition from local banks and the Bank of China," analyst Elan Cohen says in a research note.
Cohen says Hang Seng was many years away from significant growth in China and should welcome a strategic stake by a well-connected Chinese enterprise.
Speculation over this has been driving the bank's share price higher in recent days.
But even if this is factored in, current valuations cannot be justified on a stand-alone basis.
Cohen notes, however, that Hang Seng does possess superior fundamentals with an unrivalled local franchise, strong capital base, high quality assets and low cost/income ratio.
But on the key valuation driver, relative EPS growth, Hang Seng is trading at 22 times JP Morgan's 1997 forecast EPS of HK$4.99.
Cohen says that on a 12-month basis, fair value for Hang Seng's share price would be HK$100, implying a valuation of around 18 times 1998 forecast EPS of HK$5.48.
"On this basis, we believe the current premium is excessive and we advise reducing exposure to Hang Seng Bank," the note ends.
Hang Seng shares were last quoted at HK$110.50 on June 26 before market holidays related to the handover of Hong Kong by Britain to China.
